messages:
Marie: quick thought — what if we reify the admission/windowing boundary into a small conduit abstraction (i'm calling it 'conveyor') so the runloop only deals with slots and the conveyor handles window shaping + eviction hints? :thinking:
Oleg: curious. want a sketch of responsibilities? admission currently decides slot grants + window placement. conveyor would sit between admission and executor?
Marie: exactly. admission = who/when gets tokens. conveyor = how tokens are grouped into emit-ready windows, plus soft-evict signals and late-join handling. reduces coupling in the runloop.
Sam: +1 on separation, but watch telemetry. we rely on end-to-end metrics from enqueue->emit. splitting adds hop and instrumentation gaps.
Katie: operational tradeoffs: migration complexity and perf. extra hop could add ~50-150ns per request in hot path if not careful. but it lets us experiment with window heuristics without touching admission.
Ben: also think about correctness: reordering guarantees. conveyor must preserve per-request ordering where required (we have some clients that rely on monotonic ordering across microbatches). can we keep conveyor lock-free?
Marie: design note: conveyor exposes a tiny API: `claim_slot(request_meta) -> conveyor_token` and `drain(conveyor_token) -> ready_batch_id` plus `hint_eviction(batch_id, priority)`. admission implements claim_slot and hands token to conveyor.
Oleg: prototype idea: conveyor keeps compact per-lane ring buffers keyed by sequence group. small evictable frames, prefetchable K/V cache pointers. That avoids moving payloads — conveyor stores indices.
Sam: love storing indices. avoids memcpy. But we must update tracing: add `conveyor.enqueue_time` and `conveyor.emit_time` tags so SLO attribution stays meaningful.
Katie: fallback story? If conveyor misbehaves or is overloaded we should allow admission to bypass conveyor and do naive windowing (current behavior). i.e., feature flag + gradual rollout, fallback path built-in.
Ben: one more: consistency across deployments (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private). conveyor config needs to be runtime-configurable (max_window_ms, soft_threshold_pct) and exported to Console so customers can pin settings.
infra-bot: deploy-bot: new conveyor prototype branch pushed: `conveyor/prototype-1` — CI green, bench numbers in summary: ~0.9x baseline tail p99 for small requests, ~1.05x for 512-token tails (see link). :rocket:
Marie: thanks infra-bot. next steps: 1) short RFC doc with API + invariants, 2) perf microbench harness (index-based path), 3) telemetry plan + fallback rollout. volunteers?
Oleg: I'll own prototype doc + ring-buffer sketch.
Sam: i'll add tracing/telemetry hooks and help with bench harness.
Katie: I'll cook up rollout plan and console knobs for config exposure.
Ben: will validate ordering invariants and write unit tests for bypass path.
Marie: awesome. keep notes here — small messages as we iterate. maybe a short async RFC by EOD Friday? thanks. :thumbsup:
